historical_reviews.deepseek: Provides useful backend telemetry but cannot demonstrate what BMC Web renders, whether filters hide entries or how TEMP_M2 maps to the installed M.2 device.

historical_reviews.history: Rows 1067 and 1617 share only the code; their SEL-allocation and LED-control purposes, commands and classifications are excluded from this sensor-page variant.
historical_reviews.v3_1: TEMP_M2 may denote one board sensor, an aggregate zone or a slot-dependent resource. The review must join the rendered label to the approved M.2 population and physical mapping before a plausible temperature can be treated as relevant evidence.

original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC Web Sensor List displays the correct TEMP_M2 resource for the installed M.2 topology and that its identity, live temperature, units, health, thresholds and freshness match the approved platform SPEC.
original_method: Open the verified BMC-Web Sensor List through a protected session, record page/filter/pagination/refresh context, locate every applicable TEMP_M2 entry, map it to installed M.2 hardware using the SPEC, capture complete rendered details, compare fields and range, optionally correlate a supported backend read, and preserve evidence without clearing logs or changing thermal state.
manual_activity: An authorized reviewer opens the protected BMC Web UI, confirms the rendered TEMP_M2 row and visible context against the approved SPEC and M.2 mapping, and owns the final verdict; automation may capture and parse supporting evidence.
required_inputs: Installed M.2 population and slot map
Expected fields, units, status, thresholds and valid range
safety_requirements: Do not change thresholds, fan policy, power or M.2 state
Verify target, route and SPEC revision
Capture filters, sort, pagination and refresh state
Do not accept truncated SDR output
Do not use duplicate-code SEL or LED semantics
Record missing, duplicate and stale entries explicitly
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, UI route, SPEC and M.2 topology
Open and capture Sensor List context
Locate and parse applicable TEMP_M2 entry
Validate identity, mapping, reading, units, health, thresholds and timestamp
Correlate approved backend data if available
Archive redacted UI/raw evidence without verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve absent, duplicate, stale or mismapped sensor

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The ipmitool read is a possible backend cross-check but cannot replace the source BMC-Web view; its `head -100` fallback can hide the target and it lacks M.2 mapping and SPEC fields.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the protected BMC-Web Sensor List as primary evidence, capture the complete TEMP_M2 row/details and compare against the approved M.2 topology and SPEC; run a supported full backend read only to correlate the same resource.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The read-only BMC-Web check and 3/3-minute estimate remain; generic clearing and backend-only substitution are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Link a timestamped UI capture to a comparison row containing page context, physical M.2 identity, TEMP_M2 label/member, reading, unit, health, thresholds, freshness and SPEC result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit topology and UI-state evidence to the source's one-line visual check while retaining human confirmation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A backend sensor response cannot prove the Web UI exposes the correct field, refreshes it, labels the right M.2 device or avoids filter/pagination omission.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: If the platform exposes only a board-zone temperature rather than per-device telemetry, the vendor SPEC must define what installed M.2 hardware that zone represents.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define TEMP_M2 semantics and expected display fields for the exact topology. The duplicate code does not permit importing SEL allocation or LED-control expectations. A supported API can corroborate but not replace the UI acceptance unless an approved Engineering Decision says so.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/firmware/Web route, SPEC revision and installed M.2 topology
Protected session/client details with secrets redacted
Complete TEMP_M2 UI capture/export and page filter/pagination/refresh context
Physical/zone mapping, reading, unit, health, thresholds, timestamp and SPEC comparison
Approved backend correlation or documented absence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, BMC-Web procedure and SPEC-match criterion coherently target TEMP_M2 display validation. The generic log-clear instruction and DeepSeek backend substitution are method/reference defects rather than competing Master outcomes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Web route, SPEC, M.2 mapping and reviewer are identifiable inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if TEMP_M2 cannot be associated with the installed hardware or the rendered fields cannot be compared unambiguously.

review_improvement: Preserves the user-visible Web requirement, isolates three duplicate-code identities and defines a population-aware, freshness-aware thermal oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: UI correctness is not implied by backend correctness: the page can mislabel, cache, filter or omit a valid sensor. Conversely, a plausible displayed value is meaningless without physical M.2 mapping and freshness. The evidence must therefore bind UI context, sensor identity, topology and SPEC at the same observation time.
